symbols.name: chunk width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two interchanged address chunks.
symbols.quote: it swaps two disjoint address fields, chunks, of $u$ bits each in an array of $V$ stored bits (the volume) in $O(Vu^\tau)$ time on fixed tapes

symbols.name: array volume
symbols.meaning: The number of bits stored in the array.
symbols.quote: it swaps two disjoint address fields, chunks, of $u$ bits each in an array of $V$ stored bits (the volume) in $O(Vu^\tau)$ time on fixed tapes

symbols.name: saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed exponent below 1 in the cost, equal to 1 - 2^{-50}.
symbols.quote: where $\tau=1-2^{-50}$ is the saving exponent.

symbols.name: prefix
symbols.meaning: The part of an address before the first chunk.
symbols.quote: An address is $(p,h,g,d,z)$ with prefix $p$, chunks $h$ and $d$, gap $g$, suffix $z$; the goal is $(p,h,g,d,z)\mapsto(p,d,g,h,z)$.

symbols.name: first chunk
symbols.meaning: The first of the two address chunks being interchanged.
symbols.quote: An address is $(p,h,g,d,z)$ with prefix $p$, chunks $h$ and $d$, gap $g$, suffix $z$; the goal is $(p,h,g,d,z)\mapsto(p,d,g,h,z)$.

symbols.name: gap
symbols.meaning: The part of an address between the two chunks.
symbols.quote: An address is $(p,h,g,d,z)$ with prefix $p$, chunks $h$ and $d$, gap $g$, suffix $z$; the goal is $(p,h,g,d,z)\mapsto(p,d,g,h,z)$.

symbols.name: second chunk
symbols.meaning: The second of the two address chunks being interchanged.
symbols.quote: An address is $(p,h,g,d,z)$ with prefix $p$, chunks $h$ and $d$, gap $g$, suffix $z$; the goal is $(p,h,g,d,z)\mapsto(p,d,g,h,z)$.

symbols.name: suffix
symbols.meaning: The part of an address after the second chunk.
symbols.quote: An address is $(p,h,g,d,z)$ with prefix $p$, chunks $h$ and $d$, gap $g$, suffix $z$; the goal is $(p,h,g,d,z)\mapsto(p,d,g,h,z)$.

symbols.name: digit radix
symbols.meaning: The fixed prime that is the radix of the digits.
symbols.quote: Digits are radix $q$, a fixed prime.

symbols.name: chunk digit count
symbols.meaning: The number of radix-q digits in a chunk.
symbols.quote: Let each chunk have $e=m^k$ digits, with $k$ recursion levels.

symbols.name: recursion levels
symbols.meaning: The number of recursion levels, with e = m^k.
symbols.quote: Let each chunk have $e=m^k$ digits, with $k$ recursion levels.

symbols.name: vertex matrix
symbols.meaning: The rational m by m matrix carried by a terminal or gate of the network.
symbols.quote: The [Linear exchange network with restored scratch wires](exchange-network.md) has $W$ wires; each terminal and gate carries a rational $m\times m$ matrix $M$, and edge $i$ carries $A_i=M_{\mathrm{head}(i)}-M_{\mathrm{tail}(i)}$, with $s=\sum_i\operatorname{rank}A_i$.

symbols.name: edge matrix
symbols.meaning: The difference of the matrices at the head and tail of edge i.
symbols.quote: The [Linear exchange network with restored scratch wires](exchange-network.md) has $W$ wires; each terminal and gate carries a rational $m\times m$ matrix $M$, and edge $i$ carries $A_i=M_{\mathrm{head}(i)}-M_{\mathrm{tail}(i)}$, with $s=\sum_i\operatorname{rank}A_i$.

symbols.name: edge index
symbols.meaning: The index of an edge of the network.
symbols.quote: The [Linear exchange network with restored scratch wires](exchange-network.md) has $W$ wires; each terminal and gate carries a rational $m\times m$ matrix $M$, and edge $i$ carries $A_i=M_{\mathrm{head}(i)}-M_{\mathrm{tail}(i)}$, with $s=\sum_i\operatorname{rank}A_i$.

symbols.name: wire index
symbols.meaning: The index of an input wire of the network.
symbols.quote: The shear contract: input wire $w$ is routed to an output role $\rho(w)$ with $M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}=I_m$, the identity, and $s<Wm$ by [Nested subspace labels and rank deficit](subspace-labels.md).

symbols.name: role map
symbols.meaning: The map sending input wire w to its output role.
symbols.quote: The shear contract: input wire $w$ is routed to an output role $\rho(w)$ with $M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}=I_m$, the identity, and $s<Wm$ by [Nested subspace labels and rank deficit](subspace-labels.md).

symbols.name: identity
symbols.meaning: The m by m identity matrix.
symbols.quote: The shear contract: input wire $w$ is routed to an output role $\rho(w)$ with $M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}=I_m$, the identity, and $s<Wm$ by [Nested subspace labels and rank deficit](subspace-labels.md).

symbols.name: address shear
symbols.meaning: The array permutation moving the entry at address (H,D) to (H+MD,D).
symbols.quote: Let $\Phi_M$ move the entry at address $(H,D)$ to $(H+MD,D)$; then $\Phi_{M'}\Phi_M=\Phi_{M'+M}$.

symbols.name: wire input
symbols.meaning: The physical input array of wire w.
symbols.quote: Read wire $w$'s input $f_w$ as the logical array $\Phi_{-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}}f_w$.

symbols.name: stream row
symbols.meaning: The row number within a role stream.
symbols.quote: Rows are split into role streams by [Elementary stream operations](stream-ops.md): row $Wx+w-1$ goes to stream $w$ as row $x$.

symbols.name: recursion level
symbols.meaning: The index of a recursion level in the unrolled recurrence.
symbols.quote: Unrolled over the recursion levels $j$, $F_k=O(\sum_{j=0}^k (s/W)^j)$.

derivations.quote:
Suppose a row field ahead of both chunks has length divisible by $W^k$. Rows are split into role streams by [Elementary stream operations](stream-ops.md): row $Wx+w-1$ goes to stream $w$ as row $x$. Each stream has volume $V/W$ and row count divisible by $W^{k-1}$. Read wire $w$'s input $f_w$ as the logical array $\Phi_{-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}}f_w$. By the composition rule and the contract, the output is $f'_{\rho(w)}=\Phi_{M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}}\Phi_{-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}}f_w=\Phi_{I_m}f_w$. Merging rows back undoes $\rho$, giving $H\gets H+D$ on every original row.

Each smaller call acts on volume $V/W$; splitting, merging, gates and scheduling cost $O(V)$ here. So the time per unit volume $F_k$ at width $m^k$ obeys $F_0=O(1)$, $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$, the recurrence of [Recursive power saving](rank-recurrence.md). Unrolled over the recursion levels $j$, $F_k=O(\sum_{j=0}^k (s/W)^j)$. If $s/W\le1$ this is at most $k+1=O(m^{k\tau})$; otherwise it is $O((s/W)^k)$, below $m^{k\tau}$. So $F_k=O(e^\tau)$. The saving is a power of $e$ since $s/W$ is a fixed constant below $m$ but near it, so $\tau\approx1$.

For large $e$, put $k'=\lceil\log_m eceil$, the number of levels needed, and let $
u=\lceil k'\log W/(2\log q)ceil$ be the number of top digits of each chunk set aside, so $q^{2
u}\ge W^{k'}$, $1\le
u<e$ and $
u=O(\log 2e)$. Split each chunk into its top digits and rest, $h^+,h^-$ and $d^+,d^-$. Interchange the high digits and move $h^+$ next to $d^+$: $(h^+,h^-,g,d^+,d^-)$ becomes $(d^+,h^+,h^-,g,d^-)$. Now $d^+,h^+$ form a row field of range $\Lambda=q^{2
u}\ge W^{k'}$ before both remaining chunks. Pad with zero rows to $\Lambda'=W^{k'}\lceil \Lambda/W^{k'}ceil<2\Lambda$ rows, so the volume stays below $2V$.

Write the remaining width in base $m$: $e-
u=\sum_{j=0}^{k'}a_jm^j$ with $0\le a_j<m$, where the base-$m$ digit $a_j$ is the number of pieces of width $m^j$ into which each remaining chunk is cut. Interchange corresponding pieces. The total is $O(V)\sum_ja_jm^{j	au}\le O(V)\,m\sum_jm^{j	au}=O(Ve^	au)$, since $m^{k'}<me$ makes $\sum_jm^{j	au}$ a geometric sum. Scan away padded rows and reverse the joining, giving $(d^+,d^-,g,h^+,h^-)$ at cost $O(V
u)=O(Ve^	au)$.
